event: Nala: "Then we have a plan for the morning."
Anselm sets out bread, cheese and a jug of small beer on the shrine's table, and makes up a pallet.

changes.note: Bread, cheese and small beer at the shrine, and a night's sleep

memory.fact: Anselm keeps bread, hard cheese and small beer at the shrine, and shares them gladly.
Anselm keeps bread, hard cheese and small beer at the shrine, and shares them gladly.

event: Nala sleeps. The black stair comes nearer than it ever has. She wakes before dawn.

memory.fact: On day twenty-eight's night the stair dream comes nearest yet; Nala wakes before dawn.
On day twenty-eight's night the stair dream comes nearest yet; Nala wakes before dawn.

event: At first light she finds Dray at his house, and Hob at his forge on the ford road. Hawise comes too.

memory.fact: Hob's smithy is an open-fronted stone shed on the ford road, its forge glowing at the back.
Hob's smithy is an open-fronted stone shed on the ford road, its forge glowing at the back.

event: She tells them of the tidepool, the Warped ewes, the plug, and Maud's cold iron ring.
Dray: "Then we ring it." To Hob: "Stakes. As many as she needs. Start now."

memory.fact: Told of the tidepool, Dray bids Hob forge the stakes at once, and asks the Ford for old iron.
Told of the tidepool, Dray bids Hob forge the stakes at once, and asks the Ford for old iron.

event: Hob scratches his beard. "I've cold iron for twenty. The rest means melting old iron down."

memory.fact: Hob has cold iron in stock for some twenty forearm-long stakes; the rest needs old iron melted down.
Hob has cold iron in stock for some twenty forearm-long stakes; the rest needs old iron melted down.

event: Dray: "I'll ask the Ford for old nails and charms. The valley purse pays."

memory.fact: Dray says the valley purse pays for Hob's cold-iron stakes.
Dray says the valley purse pays for Hob's cold-iron stakes.
Folk at the Ford would give old cold-iron nails and charms for the stakes, if the Reeve asks.

event: Hob: "Ten by dusk, if I sweat."

memory.fact: Hob starts the stakes at once on day twenty-nine; the first ten are ready by dusk.
Hob starts the stakes at once on day twenty-nine; the first ten are ready by dusk.

event: Hob, to Nala: "Stakes in a pool bed want driving with a sledge. Someone stood right over them."

memory.fact: Hob warns that stakes in a pool bed must be driven with a sledge, by someone standing over them.
Hob warns that stakes in a pool bed must be driven with a sledge, by someone standing over them.

event: Dray sends Rob Reed riding for the Keep with word of the tidepool, and of Maud.

memory.fact: Dray sends Rob Reed to the Keep with word of the tidepool and of Maud; two Pells carry stakes up.
Dray sends Rob Reed to the Keep with word of the tidepool and of Maud; two Pells carry stakes up.

event: Dray: "The Pells will carry the stakes up as they come off the anvil."

memory.fact: Dray's watch is four untalented spearmen: Col Ashby, Rob Reed, and the Pell twins.

event: Nala and Hawise climb back up to Callow Beck. The bank at the gully mouth still holds.

memory.fact: By dusk the bank across the gully mouth holds the black slick back.
By dusk the bank across the gully mouth holds the black slick back.

event: Behind it, the black lies knee-deep in a pool forty paces up the gully.

memory.fact: Behind the bank the black lies in a knee-deep pool forty paces up the gully, some forty barrels.
Behind the bank the black lies in a knee-deep pool forty paces up the gully, some forty barrels.

event: Above that, the gully bed is crusted grey with salt, black water lying in its hollows.

memory.fact: Above that pool the gully's bed is crusted grey salt, with a few barrels of black in its hollows.
Above that pool the gully's bed is crusted grey salt, with a few barrels of black in its hollows.
The gully's grey crust is dead salt and harms nothing; rain will wash it faintly down the beck.

event: Nala kneels at the bank and begins to part the black, a cupful at a time, as on the cwm.

changes.note: Parting the black behind the bank, a cupful at a time, into the day

event: After an hour the pool behind the bank looks no different.
She sounds its size with her tide. Forty barrels at least, and more in the hollows above.
Cupful by cupful, this would take her weeks.

memory.fact: Parting the gully pool a cupful at a time would take Nala weeks of fine work.
Parting the gully pool a cupful at a time would take Nala weeks of fine work.

event: Near noon Maud comes up the track on foot, stiff and puffing, Anselm at her elbow.

memory.fact: Near noon on day twenty-nine Maud reaches the gully mouth on foot, stiff and puffing, with Anselm.
Near noon on day twenty-nine Maud reaches the gully mouth on foot, stiff and puffing, with Anselm.
